'''R2-A5''' was a [[Color/Legends|white-and-green]] plated [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2-series astromech droid]]<ref name="CCG" /> manufactured by [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]].<ref name="SWE" /> The [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] served the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], and was [[Programmer/Legends|programmed]] by the Empire for target acquisition and combat communications. Around the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], R2-A5 wandered the streets of [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]],<ref name="CSWE" /> a [[City/Legends|city]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope">{{Film|IV}}</ref> R2-A5 coordinated [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] attack vectors, and broadcasted target acquisition data to [[Gunner/Legends|gunnery]] systems.<ref name="CCG" />

==Behind the scenes==
R2-A5 first appeared in the [[1977]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], before being replaced with a CGI [[Ronto/Legends|ronto]] in the [[1997]] [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]] re-release of the film. The [[Droid/Legends|droid's]] scene, where it rolls through the streets as Tatooine locals [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] are apprehended by [[Desert stormtrooper/Legends|sandtroopers]],<ref name="Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope" /> was filmed between [[April 12]] to [[April 22]], [[1976]] at [[Elstree Studios]]'s Stage 6.<ref name="MakingOf">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref> In [[1998]], the droid was first named by [[Decipher]], for the ''[[Special Edition Limited]]'' set of their [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]].<ref name="CCG" />
